name: Potassium citrate
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Potassium citrate is a urinary alkalinizer for stone prevention (hypocitraturia, renal tubular acidosis with stones, uric acid stones). Each 1,080 mg tablet supplies 10 mEq of potassium. The US label contraindicates it when GFR is below 0.7 mL/kg/min (about 35 mL/min at 50 kg) and in hyperkalemia and in conditions that predispose to it, including chronic renal failure, and stops it if serum creatinine rises significantly.
kidney_function_basis: Label contraindication: GFR <0.7 mL/kg/min (about 35 mL/min at 50 kg, 49 mL/min at 70 kg), and any condition predisposing to hyperkalemia including chronic renal failure.
chip: CI if GFR <0.7 mL/kg/min or CKD

bands.recommendation: Severe hypocitraturia: start 60 mEq/day (30 mEq twice daily or 20 mEq three times daily) with meals; mild to moderate: start 30 mEq/day; avoid above 100 mEq/day (label). Check electrolytes, creatinine and blood count every 4 months.

Contraindicated when GFR is below 0.7 mL/kg/min (multiply by body weight: 50 kg = 35 mL/min; 70 kg = 49 mL/min) (label 4). Above that, use only with specialist input, potassium checks within 1 week of starting and of any dose change, and no potassium-sparing drugs. The label also says to avoid it in chronic renal failure and to stop it if creatinine rises significantly.

Contraindicated: GFR below 0.7 mL/kg/min, and hyperkalemia or conditions predisposing to it, including chronic renal failure (label 4, 5.1). Potentially fatal hyperkalemia can develop rapidly and silently.

crrt.text: Contraindicated: acute kidney injury and acute dehydration predispose to hyperkalemia (label).

dialyzable: Potassium is removed by dialysis (physiology; label lists hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis among hyperkalemia treatments).
monitoring: Serum potassium, sodium, chloride, carbon dioxide, creatinine and complete blood count every 4 months; more often with heart or kidney disease or acidosis. Periodic ECG. Urinary citrate and pH. Stop for hyperkalemia, significant creatinine rise or fall in hemoglobin (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and effectiveness in children not established (label).
